title: LEFT: Learnable Fusion of Tri-view Tokens for Unsupervised Time Series Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Unsupervised time series anomaly detection seeks to identify abnormal timestamps without annotation availability, including anomalies that may be subtle within any single representation.

gap.claim: Most cross-view methods use feature or score fusion without enforcing analysis-synthesis consistency between frequency and time representations.

contributions.claim: LEFT is a unified unsupervised TSAD framework that models anomalies as inconsistencies across complementary representations.
LEFT learns frequency, time-domain, and multi-scale tokens, using adaptive Nyquist-constrained spectral filters to encode multiple resolutions.
LEFT combines coarse-to-fine reconstruction of fine-grained targets with a time-frequency cycle consistency constraint to regularize cross-view agreement.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the fusion objective as novel and the time-frequency cycle consistency constraint as innovative.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames unsupervised TSAD as detecting abnormal timestamps without annotations.
It identifies subtle cross-view anomalies and limitations in existing fusion methods.
LEFT represents the same series through frequency, time, and multi-scale tokens.
The framework uses coarse-to-fine reconstruction and time-frequency cycle consistency to coordinate views.

source_observation.claim: Anomalies may be detectable through inconsistencies across complementary views even when deviations within one view are subtle.

interpretation.claim: Cross-view representation agreement can be treated as a modeling signal for unsupervised anomaly detection.

application.claim: For related multi-representation detection tasks, consider jointly modeling complementary views with an explicit agreement or consistency objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that explicit cross-view consistency improves performance across datasets or anomaly types.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are reported.
Training, inference, computational cost, and ablation details are not provided.
The abstract does not specify how anomalies are scored or thresholds are selected.
